title: Face To Face At The Mountain

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord spoke to you face to face out of the fire on the mountain. (At that time I stood between the Lord and you to declare to you the word of the Lord, because you were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain.) And he said: - Deut 5:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses reminds the people of the awesome day when God spoke from the fire. God came near — "face to face" — yet the people trembled and could not bear it. So Moses stood in the gap, a mediator between a holy God and a frightened people, carrying God's word down to them. Notice the tension in these two verses: God draws near in relationship, yet His holiness is so overwhelming that sinful people cannot approach Him directly. They needed someone to stand between.

This is one of the great threads running through the whole Bible. We long to know God closely, but our sin makes His pure holiness dangerous to us. We need a mediator. Moses filled that role for a moment, but he was only a shadow of the One to come.

Jesus is the Mediator we truly need — not standing at the foot of a burning mountain, but nailed to a cross. Through Him, the fire that once kept people back becomes a welcome. The book of Hebrews says we have not come to a mountain of fire and terror, but to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant (Heb 12:18-24). Because He stood in the gap, you can now draw near to God with confidence, not fear.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I sense both God's nearness and His holiness when I come to Him?
- What does it mean to me that Jesus stands between me and God?
- Am I coming to God through Christ, or trying to approach Him on my own terms?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Jesus stood in the gap so that I could draw near without fear. I could never approach Your holiness on my own, so I come through my Mediator, trusting His finished work. Amen.
